note: Tests that fail on the Linux runner for reasons that do not exist on this Mac. The Mac allowlist (unit-known-red.json) does NOT transfer: it names this machine's environment, and the nightly runs ubuntu-24.04-arm. An entry here is a claim with evidence, not a mute button — check it with `node local/check-nightly-linux-parity.mjs --failures <downloaded-artifacts>`, which fails on any red that is not listed and reports a listed test that passed as prunable. An entry stores Vitest's full name, describe chain included, and pins the cause with `match`; a bare title no longer absorbs anything, and an entry with no `match` that is not `flaky: true` is a problem. The 2026-11-05 upstream move of this file (2f217b4d0dd) left its entry naming a path no report contains, so the red it exists to absorb was not being absorbed at all until #317 corrected the path, the name and the cause together. 2026-11-24: `entries` is empty because upstream #46786 retired all five files it named; an empty list is the fail-closed state — every Linux shard red now fails its job until a red is classified with evidence. The five are in `prunedSince` with that reason.

Passed in every run since: 40695078222 (dispatch, nplez1/main @d96a57ffc6 — shard 3 green; that run failed only shard 1's cooldown assertion), 40701735011 (dispatch, nplez1/main @1776dcc575, all five shards) and 40797794635 (dispatch, nplez1/main @fdd5850d0f, all five shards), the last two also reporting it as a prunable entry. Every file in the stack is upstream-owned with zero fork hunks: daemon-pty-event-subscriptions.ts, daemon/client.ts, daemon-client-pending-requests.ts, daemon-pty-adapter.ts and the test itself. unhandledErrors.evidence: monaco-editor's own CancellationError raised when the editor is disposed; the stack names no repository file and no test. Observed on both machines, in runs whose only named failures were already triaged.

LOCAL-PATCHES.md records a node-runtime worker dying mid-run on this pool; it names no test, and the run it came from had every named failure already triaged. The Mac manifest carries the same headline, but only this entry sets `explainsFailure: false`: the shard verdict judges a Linux shard against its assignment, and a worker that died can lose tests inside a file the report still lists, so a crash cannot be the only explanation for a failed shard — it is tolerable only beside a known red that already explains the exit. `local/gate-unit.mjs` does not read the field.

The browser-mode dev server cannot serve Monaco's TypeScript worker from the dependency store — the URL embeds the store path, which differs per machine and per runner. No repository file appears in it and no test asserts on it.
